builder_plan.scenario: An agent reads external documents or tool responses that may contain malicious instructions.
builder_plan.change: Replay attacks and legitimate lookalikes in an isolated copy of your agent workflow.
builder_plan.baseline: Your existing checks with the same tasks, permissions, and tool responses.
steps: Locate the paper's implementation and check its license, model support, data needs, and hardware requirements. Stop here if you cannot obtain the required artifacts.
Save a small set of representative product tasks and expected outcomes. Keep evaluation tasks out of any training or tuning, and choose quality and cost limits before running.
Run the baseline and the proposed change on identical inputs. Keep other settings fixed and repeat paired runs to expose variation.
Save per-task outputs, failures, timings, and all usage costs. Review regressions before expanding the test.
builder_plan.measure: Successful attacks missed, legitimate actions blocked, detection delay, and review cost.
builder_plan.decision: Keep the change only if it meets your preselected quality and latency limits and improves the metric you care about after setup and operating costs. Otherwise retain the baseline. This is an exploration plan, not a validated recommendation.

title: Soteria: Formally Verified Planning with Runtime Enforcement for Safe LLM Agents
summary: The method replaces ad hoc reactive guardrails or post-hoc rejection with a pre-execution formal verification step against explicit specifications, followed by runtime enforcement that uses the verified plan to guide recovery when actions are blocked. It costs additional planning and verification latency, requires formalizable domain specifications, and adds integration complexity for the plan checker and monitor. It can fail if policies are incomplete or mis-specified, the verifier or environment model is unsound, or the agent cannot find a compliant recovery path.
rationale: For a small production team, the approach is promising but depends on formal specification quality and agent stack integration, so it should be validated on the reader's own tool-use workload before adoption.
technique: Verified hierarchical planning with runtime enforcement for agents

claims.statement: The method replaces ad hoc reactive guardrails or post-hoc rejection with a pre-execution formal verification step against explicit specifications, followed by runtime enforcement that uses the verified plan to guide recovery when actions are blocked. It costs additional planning and verification latency, requires formalizable domain specifications, and adds integration complexity for the plan checker and monitor. It can fail if policies are incomplete or mis-specified, the verifier or environment model is unsound, or the agent cannot find a compliant recovery path.
Soteria achieves 1.7x the average task success rate of the best baselines with no policy violations.
